name: Chicken Katsu Curry

ingredients.name: Japanese curry roux
ingredients.original: 1 x 92 g packet Japanese curry roux

steps: Rinse the rice until the water runs clear. Put it in a saucepan with 450 ml of cold water, bring to the boil, then cover, turn the heat to its lowest and cook for 12 minutes. Take it off the heat and leave it covered for 10 minutes, then fluff with a fork and keep warm (a rice cooker with the same rice and water works too).
Halve each chicken breast horizontally, then pound the pieces between sheets of baking paper to about 1 cm thick. Season the chicken all over with salt and pepper.

Set up three shallow bowls: the plain flour in one, the eggs beaten in the second, the panko breadcrumbs in the third. Coat each piece of chicken in flour, dip in egg, then press firmly into the panko so the crumbs stick. Set aside.

Heat 1 tablespoon of the vegetable oil in a saucepan over medium heat. Dice the brown onion and crush the garlic, then cook them for 5 minutes until soft. Peel and chop the carrots and potatoes into bite-sized chunks, add them to the pan and stir for 2 minutes.

Add the chicken stock and bring it to the boil, then simmer for 12 minutes or until the vegetables are tender. Take the pan off the heat, break in the Japanese curry roux and stir until dissolved, then simmer for 3 minutes more until thick and glossy.

Meanwhile, get a large frying pan hot over medium-high heat with the remaining vegetable oil, until a pinch of panko sizzles straight away. Fry the chicken in two batches for 3-4 minutes each side until deep golden and cooked through. Drain on a wire rack and rest for a few minutes.
Slice the katsu into strips. Divide the rice between bowls, ladle the curry over one side and top with the sliced chicken.
